author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction updates that same visit and never adds a second visit to the pet. It follows the same validation rules as booking.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is requested, then the visit form is shown prefilled with that visit's current date and description

given a booked visit, when a non-blank description and a date later than today are POSTed to the same URL, then that visit is updated in place, the pet's visit count is unchanged, and the response redirects to the owner detail page
given a booked visit, when the correction carries a blank description, then the form is redisplayed with the description named and the stored visit is unchanged
given a booked visit, when the correction carries a date of today or earlier, then the form is redisplayed with the date named and the stored visit is unchanged
given a visitId that does not exist or does not belong to the named pet and owner, when the edit URL is requested, then the request is refused rather than showing or changing another visit
non_goals: Any edit link or other visible entry point on the owner detail page; the owner deferred it to a possible follow-up request
Correcting any visit field other than date and description, including which pet it belongs to
notes: Owner constraints from the intake: reuse the existing template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its `visit` model attribute; validation identical to creation (description required, date in the future). Docs written this dispatch: docs/prd.md (REQ-VIS-003, NG-5 row, preamble, Open Questions), new docs/adr/2026-10-25-non-goal-visit-cancellation-only.md, and a Status amendment on docs/adr/2026-08-08-non-goal-deletion-and-visit-amendment.md. docs/adr/README.md Index needs a row for the new ADR; that file is outside product write scope. Open questions recorded in the PRD and not blocking: a visible entry point (deferred by the owner); past visits must move their date forward to be corrected, a consequence of 'validates like visit creation'. Edge case 3 (unknown or mismatched visitId is refused) is the narrowest reading; the owner did not state it.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction follows the child-edit pattern PetController already demonstrates (resolve the existing child through the Owner root, change it, save the Owner; system-design.md Contracts invariants: Owner is the aggregate entry point, no VisitRepository). The adjustment: VisitController's @ModelAttribute("visit") today always constructs a new Visit and attaches it to the pet on every handler, so an edit route mapped beside it would bind the form onto a fresh visit and the cascade save would insert a second one. The model-attribute method must branch on an optional visitId path variable, as PetController.findPet branches on petId: present -> resolve owner, then pet, then that pet's visit by id (new Pet lookup in Pet.java) and refuse if any is missing; absent -> today's new-visit behavior unchanged. Grep basis (IDE oracle not connected): VisitController.loadPetWithVisit, PetController.findPet/updatePetDetails, Owner.getPet(Integer), Pet.addVisit. The future-date rule is the same rule creation applies and stays in VisitController under the recorded Web-controller deviation (system-design.md Open Questions 2); factor it into one private check both POST handlers call, never a second copy. Docs written: Contracts rows Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, VisitController gain REQ-VIS-003; one invariant sentence; Security Context inputs and the identifier-tampering threat row name visit identifiers; new Scale and Load section with the per-pet visit lookup row; ADR index row for the NG-5 narrowing ADR, as the prd-entry notes requested.
integration_points: Entry point GET+POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, binding target: the persisted Visit resolved owner -> pet -> visit, behind an allow-list of date and description (security-principles.md Realization, Mass assignment); keep the existing id and *.id disallow. Re-resolve the whole chain on every request, including the POST (security-principles.md Realization, Trusting cross-request state).
Framework transport double: MockMvc in VisitControllerTests (the sanctioned mock, testing-principles.md Mocking Policy).

OwnerRepository double in VisitControllerTests: the existing @MockitoBean stub, kept as the suite's tolerated exception, because OwnerRepository extends JpaRepository and a hand-written fake would outweigh the assertions. Assert in place: the pet's visits collection size is unchanged and the fixture's own Visit instance carries the new values; on validation failure, save is never called.

OwnerRepository real implementation: if the in-place update needs proof against JPA merge semantics (update, not insert), add it to the existing ClinicServiceTests data-layer test against H2, not as a further stub.
Template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm reused with its visit model attribute. The form has no th:action, so it posts back to the edit URL. Its heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit.

patterns.description: findPet: model attribute branching on an optional child id path variable; updatePetDetails: change the resolved child, then save the Owner root
getPet(Integer): id lookup over persisted children, the shape for the new Pet visit lookup

risks.risk: The new-visit branch of the model attribute also runs on the edit route and adds a stray visit, breaking 'the pet gains no further visit'
risks.mitigation: Branch on the optional visitId; the edit branch never calls Pet.addVisit (system-design.md Contracts invariant: a correction attaches no new visit)

risks.risk: A visitId belonging to another pet or owner is shown or changed
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only among the named owner's pet's visits and refuse otherwise, using the same refusal the controller already raises for a missing owner or pet (system-design.md Threat Model, identifier-tampering row). The refusal message carries identifiers only (security-principles.md Realization, Secret disclosure)

risks.risk: Per-pet visit lookup scales with that pet's visits
risks.mitigation: system-design.md Scale and Load row 'One pet's visits': bounded, simplest readable form (linear scan of the eager collection)

risks.risk: Any new label (for example an update-visit button text) breaks REQ-LANG-002 if a locale bundle lacks it
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading keeps the template's text unchanged. Any new key goes into every locale bundle (system-design.md Contracts note on REQ-LANG-002)

risks.risk: Without a transaction, binding mutates the detached visit before validation; a refused correction must leave storage untouched
risks.mitigation: Return the form before any save on errors. Storage is untouched because nothing reaches OwnerRepository (system-design.md Persistence: open-in-view disabled, writes only through OwnerRepository)

notes: No ADR: the model-attribute branching is a single-slice choice with no trade-off later slices must respect. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. The NG-5 non-goal ADR and the Status amendment on the 2026-08-08 ADR are product-authored (see prd-entry line 3 notes); this dispatch wrote only the ADR index row. Open questions stay as the PRD records them: no visible entry point; past visits need a future date to be corrected.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Mass assignment: VisitController.java:55 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` adds an allow-list beside the existing `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")` (line 56). The unqualified @InitBinder applies to every binder in the controller, so the edit POST can bind only the two form fields onto the persisted Visit. It also stops request parameters from binding onto the `@ModelAttribute Owner owner` argument of both POST handlers (lines 108 and 127). That closes a path the old id-only disallow list left open, so the change strengthens the baseline. VisitControllerTests.java:240 `theVisitCorrectionShouldBindNoFieldOutsideDateAndDescription` exercises the allow-list.

Ownership / IDOR within the demo's no-auth baseline: the visit is resolved through the path's owner, then pet, then that pet's own persisted visits (Pet.java `getVisit` filters `!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id)` over `getVisits()`). A visitId belonging to another pet resolves to null and is refused (VisitController.java:86-89). Each request re-resolves the entity from the repository and trusts no state from an earlier request. Tests at VisitControllerTests.java:183 and :189 cover refusal on GET and POST.

Validation parity: the edit POST carries `@Valid Visit visit` (line 127) and calls the same `rejectDateNotInFuture` the create path calls (lines 110 and 129). The rule has one implementation, not a second copy. With `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (application.properties:11), the loaded owner graph is detached, so a failed validation leaves the store unchanged because no `save` runs.

Error output: the new IllegalArgumentException message (lines 87-88) carries only integer path ids and follows the owner and pet messages already in the method. It holds no credential or connection detail.

Output escaping: the reused template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders visit data with `th:text` only. `grep -F -n -e th:utext -r src/main/resources/templates` returned no matches. The template file is unchanged by this diff.

No injection, file I/O, shell, deserialization or logging sinks are added. The production diff touches only Pet.java and VisitController.java, and their hunks use the repository's `findById`/`save` and plain Java. No secret is added: the diff's added lines carry no credential literal.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set, so no dependency changed. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (no `dependencyCheck` match in build.gradle), so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved runtimeClasspath versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: spring-webmvc 7.0.9, spring-boot-thymeleaf 4.1.1, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.5, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.

Exposed surface: the change adds GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, open to every caller like every existing mutating route under the recorded demonstration baseline (docs/security-principles.md, What this application is). It edits only a visit's date and description. Management exposure is unchanged.
